body: On 23 Apr 2020 Franklin Templeton MF froze and wound up six credit-oriented debt schemes (incl. Franklin India Credit Risk, Ultra Short Bond, Low Duration) with ~Rs 25,215 cr AUM, citing Covid-era illiquidity and redemption pressure. Investors were locked in; after a Supreme Court-supervised liquidation by SBI MF, unitholders ultimately received ~Rs 27,508 cr, i.e., >100% of AUM at closure -- but over ~3 years, with forced illiquidity at the worst time. Visible flags: (1) schemes held concentrated, low-rated or unrated papers and structured obligations (promoter-backed loans against shares, group holdcos) that had no secondary market; (2) yields well above category -- the extra yield was liquidity and credit risk; (3) earlier losses on Vodafone Idea and Essel group paper (2019-20) and side-pocketing; (4) the schemes had to borrow to meet redemptions in Mar-Apr 2020. SEBI later penalised Franklin and barred it from launching new debt schemes for two years (2021). Lesson: a debt fund's YTM above peers is a risk measure, not a reward; check portfolio liquidity, single-issuer exposure, unrated share and borrowing; even good recovery outcomes can come with years of lock-in.

data.early_signals: unrated/structured papers; above-category YTM; side-pockets; borrowing for redemptions

title: Franklin Templeton India: six debt funds wound up (Apr 2020)
